title: U.S. House · Illinois's 3rd District
area: Parts of Chicago's Northwest and Southwest Sides and western Cook County suburbs

context.text: Incumbent Delia Ramirez (D) ran unopposed in the March 17, 2026 Democratic primary. Angel Oakley won the Republican primary unopposed.

candidates.name: Delia Ramirez
candidates.ballotNote: Ran unopposed in the March 17, 2026 Democratic primary

summary.text: Ramirez represents Illinois' 3rd Congressional District. Before Congress she served one term in the Illinois House of Representatives and worked as a community organizer and nonprofit executive.

background.text: Born in Chicago; earned a bachelor's degree in justice studies from Northeastern Illinois University.
Worked as a social services administrator, community organizer, and policy advocate; co-founded Justice for Our Neighbors (JFON).
Served as executive director of the Center for Changing Lives and board chair of the Latin United Community Housing Association and Logan Square Neighborhood Association.
Served in the Illinois House of Representatives, District 4, 2019-2023, before her election to Congress in 2022.

priorities.text: Housing is a human right, period. As a housing organizer, I know that a new future for housing is possible: one that is bold, progressive, affordable, sustainable. In Congress, I am organizing and fighting for legislation and investment to realize a progressive vision of affordable, sustainable housing for all, by tenants and for tenants.

In one of the wealthiest nations of the world, no person should have to choose between getting the care they need or staggering medical debt, buying their medication, or paying their mortgage. Health care is a human right, full stop.

Know that in me, you will always find someone who stands ready to fight for working families and to protect and support all workers' right to have fair wages, safe and dignified working conditions, universal health care, and democracy in their workplace.

positions.summary: Says she is a long-time advocate for reproductive rights and safe abortion access, and is committed to codifying Roe v. Wade into law.
positions.quote: Representative Ramirez is committed to protecting bodily autonomy and make of Roe V. Wade the law of the land through legislative fix.

positions.summary: Cosponsors gun violence prevention legislation, including Ethan's Law and the Break the Cycle of Violence Act.
positions.quote: As a co-sponsor of Ethan's Law , the Keep Americans Safe Act , and the Break the Cycle of Violence Act , she advocates for gun violence prevention policies that address the root causes of crime and programs that strengthen community violence prevention and interruption.

positions.summary: Calls for abandoning current border enforcement policies and opposes scapegoating asylum seekers, while supporting legal pathways and relief for undocumented immigrants.
positions.quote: Congresswoman Ramirez advocates we abandon the decades of failed border enforcement policies and support for ineffective initiatives and reject the scapegoating of asylees seeking safety.

positions.summary: Champions Medicare for All and led the expansion of Illinois Medicaid to cover residents regardless of immigration status.
positions.quote: As a member of the Congressional Progressive Caucus, Congresswoman Ramirez fights for the passage of the Medicare for All Act , Close the Medigap Act , and the Medicare Dental, Vision, and Hearing Benefit Act.

positions.summary: Cosponsors the Green New Deal and Climate Resilience Workforce Act and calls for ending reliance on fossil fuels.
positions.quote: Ramirez believes we must protect our sacred lands, oceans and wildernesses and end our reliance on fossil fuels.

positions.summary: Says the tax code shouldn't do more for billionaires and corporations than for working families and cosponsors the Tax Excessive CEO Pay Act.
positions.quote: Congresswoman Ramirez believes our tax code shouldn't do more for billionaires and corporations than it does for working families.

record.text: Assigned to the House Committee on Homeland Security and the House Committee on Veterans' Affairs (Subcommittees on Disability Assistance and Memorial Affairs, and Economic Opportunity) in the 118th Congress.

candidates.name: Angel Oakley
candidates.ballotNote: Ran unopposed in the March 17, 2026 Republican primary

summary.text: Oakley holds bachelor's and master's degrees from Judson University and has worked in cannabis and CBD consulting and as an adjunct instructor.

background.text: Earned a bachelor's degree and a master's degree from Judson University.
Career experience includes work as a founder, chief consultant, cannabis educator/advisor, CBD broker, and adjunct instructor.

researchNotes: Ramirez's positions and priorities are drawn from her official House issues pages. No campaign website or citable public statements were found for Angel Oakley beyond basic biographical facts.
